intent: compare current sports betting research apps
title: The best sports betting research apps for 2026
seoTitle: Best Sports Betting Research Apps for 2026
description: A documented comparison of eight sports betting research apps, with current prices, platform limits, category wins, and an honest selection guide.
dek: Eight very different research workflows, compared from current official documentation so you can choose the right tool without pretending one app wins every category.
author: chris-habib

hero.alt: WagerProof app icon in front of seven sports research app icons on a green data grid
hero.caption: Official app icons composited over an AI-assisted abstract data field. Product marks belong to their respective owners.
hero.source: Official App Store artwork retrieved 2026-08-26; WagerProof editorial composition

disclosure: WagerProof is built by Red Honey, the publisher of this guide. We ranked it first for configurable AI-agent research, but competitors win categories such as market scanning, visual prop research, tracking, editorial breadth, and no-code model building. This is a documentation-based comparison, not a hands-on test of every paid plan. We did not audit prediction accuracy.
verdict: Start with the job you need done. WagerProof is the strongest fit here for combining model-market disagreement, configurable AI agents, graded records, and saved systems. OddsJam is the clearer market-scanning specialist, Props.Cash is easier for visual prop research, Pikkit is the tracking-first choice, Action Network combines research with editorial coverage, and Rithmm is the stronger no-code model-builder.

apps.name: WagerProof
apps.price: Free limited tier; Pro pricing appears in-app and varies by region
apps.summary: Model probabilities, customizable AI agents, automatic grading, outliers, historical systems, WagerBot, and selected player-prop tools in one research workflow.
apps.whyItWins: The current product combines configurable agents, public graded records, model-to-market disagreement, and reusable historical systems rather than making you stitch those jobs together.
apps.limitation: Current iOS documentation lists models across five sports, while cross-book player props are specifically documented for MLB and NFL. Most depth is Pro-gated, and every model output remains an estimate.

apps.name: Juice
apps.price: Official March 2026 page: $6.99 weekly or $99.99 yearly after a 3-day trial; verify checkout
apps.summary: Upload a bet-slip screenshot, compare live prices, and review probability or expected-value estimates from several named AI models.
apps.whyItWins: Its official material documents the fastest screenshot-to-multi-model workflow in this group, with four named assistants shown side by side.
apps.limitation: Public material does not provide an independent calibration audit, and App Store purchase labels are not clear enough to treat every displayed amount as a billing period.

apps.name: OddsJam
apps.categoryLabel: Best for market scanning and line shopping
apps.price: Modular plans; current U.S. App Store tiers range from $19.99 monthly to $399.99 monthly
apps.summary: A broad scanning suite for line shopping, player trends, positive-EV screens, arbitrage, middles, promotional conversion, and tracking.
apps.whyItWins: OddsJam documents the broadest market-scanning and arbitrage orientation here, including coverage across a very large set of books.
apps.limitation: There is no simple all-access price, and advanced workflows can require several sportsbook accounts, substantial bankroll, and daily operating time.

apps.name: Outlier
apps.categoryLabel: Best blend of prop context and price tools
apps.price: Premium $19.99 monthly; Premium+ $29.99 monthly; Pro $79.99 monthly
apps.summary: Visual player-prop and game research with contextual stats, injuries, price comparison, movement, alerts, and higher-tier EV or arbitrage tools.
apps.whyItWins: Outlier brings useful player context and market-price tooling into the same documented workflow.
apps.limitation: Outlier says Android currently supports Premium and MLB, while several Premium+ and Pro capabilities remain web or iOS only.

apps.name: Props.Cash
apps.price: $19.99 monthly or $199.99 yearly for all sports
apps.summary: Visual prop trends, advanced filters, current lines, roster and injury context, odds analysis, and correlated-prop exploration.
apps.whyItWins: Its narrow focus produces an approachable prop-research interface with useful roster context and correlation views.
apps.limitation: It is explicitly player-prop-centric rather than a broad game-model, custom-agent, or market-arbitrage platform.

apps.name: Pikkit
apps.categoryLabel: Best for verified tracking and social records
apps.price: Core tracking free; Pro $29.99 monthly or $199.99 yearly in the U.S. App Store
apps.platforms: iPhone, Android; web access is Pro
apps.summary: BookSync aggregates verified sportsbook history into profit-and-loss, ROI, live tracking, line shopping, and community activity.
apps.whyItWins: Pikkit has the clearest tracking-first identity in the group, with automatic sync, verified records, and a built-in social layer.
apps.limitation: Pikkit does not support manual bet entry. If a sportsbook is unsupported, the wager cannot simply be added by hand. Several analysis and export features are Pro-gated.

apps.name: Action Network
apps.categoryLabel: Best for editorial breadth with odds and tracking
apps.price: Free basic product; PRO $14.99 weekly, $24.99 monthly, or $119.99 yearly
apps.summary: Live odds, line movement, scores, bet tracking, expert picks, editorial analysis, public-betting data, and alerts.
apps.whyItWins: Action Network offers the broadest documented combination of editorial coverage, odds context, alerts, and tracking in this comparison.
apps.limitation: Many useful data layers, projections, articles, and alerts require PRO, and the product is not documented as a custom no-code model builder.

apps.name: Rithmm
apps.price: Core $29.99 monthly; Pro $49.99 monthly; Premium $99.99 monthly; annual plans available
apps.summary: Model-backed props and game research with house, user-built, or community models, Smart Signals, line shopping, tracking, parlays, and Scout AI.
apps.whyItWins: Rithmm documents the strongest no-code model-building path here, from using a house model to building or copying a model and interrogating its reasoning.
apps.limitation: Scout is not included in Core and is usage-limited on higher plans. Advanced factors, player-impact adjustments, and exports require Premium.

faqs.question: What is the best sports betting research app?
faqs.answer: The best app depends on the job. WagerProof is the strongest fit in this comparison for configurable AI-agent research and graded systems. OddsJam is better suited to broad market scanning, Props.Cash to visual prop research, Pikkit to tracking, and Rithmm to no-code model building.

faqs.question: Did WagerProof test every paid plan in this comparison?
faqs.answer: No. This is a documentation-based review of official product, help, pricing, and U.S. app-store pages checked on August 26, 2026. We did not install every paid tier or independently audit prediction accuracy.

faqs.question: Can a research app guarantee profitable bets?
faqs.answer: No. Research apps can organize data, estimate probabilities, compare prices, or track decisions. Their outputs are uncertain, every wager can lose, and past records do not guarantee future results.
